label: Comic Panel Radio Adaptation

prompt_stages.outline_system: You are adapting public-domain comic panels into radio drama. Preserve page order, named characters, visible action, and ending while translating visual beats into sound and dialogue.
prompt_stages.pitch_room_system: Generate adaptation approaches for turning panels into audio beats; do not invent a replacement story.
prompt_stages.dramatic_state_system: Define the central conflict from the comic's panel sequence and character actions.
prompt_stages.line_grounding: Ground this line in the panel/page source and the current audio beat.
prompt_stages.coda_system: Write a source attribution note for the comic/page excerpt.
prompt_stages.title_system: Title the adaptation using a source-grounded visual or action detail.
prompt_stages.story_select_system: Grade public-domain adaptations for source fidelity, clear audio drama, and valid compression.
prompt_stages.style_pick_inventor: You are adapting public-domain source material for visual radio storytelling while preserving source fidelity.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser: Choose a visual style that supports the supplied public-domain source and does not replace the source with a new genre premise.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser_user_template: Choose the best visual style for this public-domain adaptation: {story_summary}

job_prompts.story_seed: You are putting drawn panels on the microphone. Name the strip's own characters and the situation the pages set up. Keep the pages in the order they were drawn. Title the episode from a visible object or action on the page. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.story_arc: Give each act one premise taken from the pages in the order they run. The last act lands the strip's own ending, its punchline as drawn, never a new one. Do not reorder pages or panels to make a cleaner arc. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.act_spine: Plan this act's spine, entry state, and exit state as planning text, not dialogue. Take the conflict from what the panels actually show these characters doing. Say what the page sequence has changed by the act's end. Do not replace a source character with one of your own.
job_prompts.act_beats: Each beat is one panel or one run of panels, in page order. Name what a listener must hear from that panel. Leave no beat that works only on the page. Beat intents are planning text, not lines.
job_prompts.act_dialogue: Ground every line in the panel it comes from and in this beat. Where a speech balloon gives a character words, carry those words as printed. Make the visible action audible: a character names what they see, hear, or do, or the moment becomes a music cue. Land the strip's punchline exactly as drawn. Carry whatever the pages contain, including their violence, as the artist drew it.
job_prompts.act_cleanup: Leave a line a speech balloon gave you exactly as it was printed. Turn a caption, a panel description, or a printed sound effect into words that same character says out loud, or into a music cue. Keep the rows in page order. Change nothing else.
job_prompts.announcer_open: Open the program like a studio announcer introducing a comic strip brought to radio. Say the title, the setting, the scene time, and each character name exactly as given. Describe nothing the listener cannot hear. Spoken words only.
job_prompts.announcer_news_coda: Speak a bridge that turns from the drama to the pages it came from, then say the supplied closing claim word for word. Land on a concrete final image from the last panel adapted. Never read a URL, a file name, or a page reference aloud.

examples: A comic page gag becomes a sequence of dialogue, sound effects, and announcer cues without showing text on screen.
source_requirements: Manifest with page text and optional image references.
ledger_validation_notes: Adaptation trace should store page ids and panel references.
